submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole is a retrospective 'spell it out' detector: it fires on a token that is a piece of a long multi-piece word - a rare, technical, proper-noun, foreign or identifier-like word that the tokenizer splits into several BPE pieces - peaking on an interior piece (Chem|oin|vest|ig|ative -> 'vest' 1.9, Ch|aler|mb|ure -> 'aler' 1.7, Sub|m|arg|inal -> 'arg' 1.5, a|theros|cl|er|otic -> 'er' 1.3, un|inform|ative -> 'inform' 1.0, Es|cher|ich|ia -> 'cher' 0.65, cerc|op|it|hec|ida|e -> 'it' 0.5, Amazon K|inesis -> 'inesis' 0.6) and it also fires on interior tokens of multi-digit numerals ('range(10)' -> '0' 0.28, '13' -> '3' 0.21, '1,204,000' -> '4' 0.24); in a matched frame that piece beats an ordinary whole word in the same slot by a wide margin (anthraquinones 0.43 vs chemicals 0.14, chrysanthemum 0.30 vs flower 0.08, cercopithecidae 0.51 vs monkey 0.07, piezophily 0.33 vs stress 0.10). Plain prose made of common single-piece words stays near its 0.03-0.15 baseline - even long single-token words are inert ('downloadable' 0.08) - with a context-dependent tail to about 0.3 on ordinary words, and it is not a next-token predictor (Jacobian-lens kurtosis 3.7, lens agreement 0%, incoherent promoted set).
